newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps all moderate gainers, bar flat fuel.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps all moderate gainers, bar flat fuel.

text.p: European oil swaps tracked higher on Thursday, but the gains were made in a generally thin market with several dealers calling it a day early.
Brent crude CFDs rose about 10 cents across the board while gasoline pegged up $2 or so on a possible swaps move. Naphtha was also up to $2 firmer taking its lead from screen crude.
Brent CFDs were pegged at -57 cents against August Brent compared with -65 cents on Thursday while June 23-27 was put at -49/48 against -55.
Further out the strength was less firm with June 30-July 4 assessed at -44 cents from -48 cents whiel July 7-11 was put at -39/40 cents under against -41 cents under.
June 30-July 4 traded at August -46 cents and July 7-11 went at August -39 cents. Dealers also said June 23-July 4 was sold at August -47.
Gas oil crack spreads were mixed with 4Q gaining to $4.60 from $4.55 but 1Q98 losing a couple of cents to $.55 from $4.58 and 2Q98 rising to $4.10 from $4.05.
Heavy fuel was fairly steady with July holding between $83.50 and $84.00 with August pegged around $84.00. Dealers said a few swaps had traded on July around $83.75.
Low sulphur fuel was pegged around $92 for July with August at 93.25, but there was little activity.
Gasoline swaps saw July trading at $185. The physical market was judged tightish, but some dealers said one heavy wet buyer had a long swaps position to play into.
Naphtha tracked $2.50 higher with crude with June put at $183.50/184.00 and July at $180.50 and August flat.
